free_tier.stated: anonymous guest read of 9 root entries; no account and no payment

egress.terms: served through cloudflare; the reader pays nothing

chaining: a fetch substrate: point a cache and two mirrors at it, never a write tier A read-only corpus, so there is no multiplication. Useful as a fetch mirror and as the reference implementation of publishing guest credentials and putting Cloudflare in front, which is the transferable part

limits.value: no published rate; one operator and a CDN front absorb the read
PUT denied at the guest role

reliability_note: The reference reader. A 7.43 TiB book and comic corpus, Cloudflare-fronted, and a 36,747,196-byte PDF read back at 206 with cf-cache-status HIT. The upstream is a SharePoint tenant, which is why single files reach tens of GiB.

evidence.proved: HTTP 200, JSON carrying a code field, site_title 'OpenList'
anonymous POST /api/fs/list on / returned code 200 with 9 root entries; write:true, write_content_bypass:False, provider:unknown
the zero-byte oracle (PUT at an existing directory with Overwrite:false) returned code 403 with message 'permission denied' inside HTTP 200, so the write permission failed and nothing was written
